4. The case of the plaintiff, in short, was that the suit jote recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 106 of mouza Arulia, District-Bogra was recorded in the name of Syed Altaf Ali Chowdhury the mautwalli of Syeda Jabedun Nesa Chowdhurani Estate and others in different shares. That in the remark column against the suit plot No. 1029 of that C.S. Khatian No. 106 the names of Altaf Ali and others were recorded with different shares. Syed Abu Mohammad Mosarraf Hossain Chowdhury the mautwalli of Syed Moazzem Hossain Chowdhury used to possess the land of suit plot No. 1029 in his khas right and the said land was also recorded in his name in his khas khatian. That the recorded Zaminders Krishno Sundari and others never possessed the land of this suit plot. That though in the C.S. Khatian, in the remark column, it was written that the pond and other land of the suit plot were being used by general public but in fact the general public never used this land and pond of the suit plot. That 1.00 acre land out 2.40 acres land of this suit plot No. 1029 was acquired by the Government. That Mosarraf Hossain Chowdhury died leaving only son Syed Mozahar Hossain Chowdhury who died leaving son the defendant No. 14 Syed Mirzarul Alam Chowdhury. That on 14.05.1994 the defendant No. 14 Syed Mirzarul Alam Chowdhury exchanged the 'Ka' scheduled 0.47 acre land of the suit plot No. 1029 with some land of the plaintiff by a registered deed of exchange and also delivered possession of the said land to the plaintiff. The plaintiff since then had been possessing the suit land on payment of rent etc. regularly. That the defendants created obstacle in the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and disclosed that their father purchased 1.36 acres of land of suit plot No. 1029-described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint by a registered kabala dated 10.11.1975 from the defendant No. 12. That the plaintiff then procured the certified copy of that alleged kabala and learnt about that alleged kabala in details. The plaintiff alleged that the said kabala of the defendant Nos. 1 to 11 is forged, collusive and inoperative and that the defendant No. 12 never executed that kabala and the defendants also never possessed the suit land. That the defendant No. 12 was very respectable person of that locality and he never went to the registry office for executing and registering the said deed. That the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1 to 11 created that kabala deed by false personification. That the said kabala deed was also unlawfully registered in Gabtoli Sub-Registry office though the land of the said kabala deed was not within the jurisdiction of Gabtoli Sub-registry office. That this impugned kabala has cast cloud upon the title of the plaintiff in the 'Ka' scheduled land and hence the suit. 

 5. The defendant No. 12 appeared in the suit and filed a written statement. This defendant has denied the genuineness of the impugned kabala deed in the name of the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1 to 11 and stated to the effect that Altaf Ali Chowdhury-one of the recorded owners of the suit land got the suit land in his exclusive share through amicable arrangement and also was in possession of that land exclusively. That Altaf Ali Chowdhury died leaving five sons among whom Mohammad Ali Chowdhury and Omar Ali Chowdhury got the land of the suit plot in their exclusive share. That Omar Ali Chowdhury the defendant No. 12 never executed the impugned deed dated 10.11.1975 in favour of Osman Gani and neither Osman Gani nor his successors ever possessed the suit land. 

 6. The defendant No. 14 also entered appearance and filed written statement sup-porting the case of the plaintiff. But ultimately this defendant No. 14 did not remain present during trial of the suit and did not adduce any evidence in support of his pleading. 

 7. The defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 5 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. Their defence case, in short, was that the properties of C.S. Khatian No. 106 was recorded in the name of Syed Altaf Ali Chowdhury and others. By amicable arrangement Syed Altaf Ali Chowdhury got the land of the suit plot in his exclusive share. That since the land of the suit plot was leased out by the Fishery Department of the Government to one Advocate objection was raised by said Syed Altaf Ali Chowdhury and ultimately the order of lease was cancelled. That the people of the locality applied before the revenue officer for acquisition of the pond of the suit land, but the said application was rejected with the finding that the said pond had not been used for cultivation. That the predecessor of this contesting defendant, namely, Osman Gani Mondol purchased the suit land from the defendant No. 12 the son of Altaf Ali Chowdhury by the impugned registered kabala dated 10.11.1975 and got possession. That one Ismail Hossain and others tried to catch fish from the suit pond forcibly for which these defendants filed a criminal case against them and they were convicted in that criminal case. That one Shamsuddin instituted Easement Case No. 80 of 1983 for establishing easement right on the suit land, but that suit was ultimately dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 23.11.1991. That the defendants have been possessing the suit land peacefully on payment of rent to the Government and the suit land has also been recorded in their names. That the defendant No. 14 Mirzarul Alam Chowdhury made an application under Rule 30 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules challenging the recording of the suit land in the name of the predecessor of the defendants but the said objection was subsequently withdrawn and the case was rejected. That the plaintiff has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. These defendants have been possessing the suit land for more than 12 years by cultivating fish in the pond of the suit land. 

 16. In this suit the plaintiff has prayed for a decree declaring a registered deed of the year 1975 as forged, inoperative and collusive. A registered deed has got a presumptive value of being genuine. This presumption no doubt, rebuttable. The party who claims a registered deed to be forged, collusive etc. the initial .onus upon that party to prove that the said registered deed is actually forged and collusive. But in this suit it appears that the plaintiff has failed to discharge this onus. The plaintiff has examined two witnesses only including himself. The trial court has discussed the evidence of these two P.Ws. in his judgment and opined rightly that the plaintiff could not adduce any evidence to prove that the impugned registered deed is forged. The trial court has considered the evidence of defendant No. 12-the executor of the impugned registered deed who was examined on commission as D.W.4. The trial court has quoted some portion of the evidence of this D.W.4 in its judgment. This D.W.4 in. cross-examination has stated that his nayeb Ahmad Ali Pramanik used to negotiate the transfers of land by him and in many cases he took the consideration money also from the purchasers. This D.W.4 has stated also that he could not remember how much land he sold and by how many deeds in the year 1975. It appears that the trial court has deeply considered the evidence of this D.W.4 who was an old man of 76 years and rightly opined that in view of the evidence of this D.W.4 it could not he held that he did not execute the impugned deed. The trial court has examined and compared the signatures of this D.W. 4 in the impugned kabala deed with his signatures in a registered kabala deed of the year 1976-the exhibit 'Ka 1' executed by this D.W.4 as per section 73 of the Evidence Act and found that both the signatures are similar. The appellate court below, of course, has made comment to the effect that this exhibit 1 ' had not been proved genuine in accordance with law. But it appears that the plaintiff-petitioner did not raise any objection as to genuineness of this exhibit-'Ka 1. In this leave petition there is no statement or submission at all questioning the genuineness of this old registered deed the exhibit Ka 1'. However, it appears that both the appellate court below and the revisional court held a very erroneous view that in this suit the onus was entirely on the contesting defendants to prove that the impugned kabala deed was a genuine one. This view of the appellate court and the High Court Division is wrong. The burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lies on that person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side. In this present suit the plaintiff sought a decree declaring an old registered kabala deed collusive, fraudulent etc. In this suit if no evidence is given from either side the suit will fail and consequently the impugned kabala deed will stand valid. In the circumstances the initial onus was on the plaintiff to prove his allegation that this registered deed was forged and collusive etc. But it appears that, as I have already mentioned above, the plaintiff has miserably failed to discharge this onus. The plaintiff did not pray even to the trial court to examine the signatures of the defendant No. 12 in the impugned kabala deed with his some admitted signatures by a handwriting expert in order to prove the alleged forgery in creating the impugned kabala deed.
